title: Adversarial code-graph fixture oracle, v0
description: Ground truth AND admissibility expectations for one adversarial fixture case. The `facts` block scores correctness (surface S2); the `admissibility` block scores honesty (surface S3). A case may fail on either independently.

language.description: Source language of this case. NOT the Gortex extractor tier -- the tier is a property of the tool at measurement time and is recorded in the result, never asserted here.

oracle_kind.description: How ground truth for this case was obtained. `constructed` means the fixture is authored so the answer holds by construction, which is what makes these cases usable where no compiler or language server exists.

independent_oracle.description: Present when a second, non-Gortex analyser can answer the same questions. Availability is a per-(language, relation) fact and must be recorded per case, never inferred from a tier.

adversarial_about.description: One paragraph: which resolution shortcut this case is built to provoke.

gold_identity.description: The anchor, bound to a fixture-held identity. A seed supplied to the tool under test must be checked against this before its expansion is scored -- otherwise a mis-identified seed turns a localization error into a fidelity result.

expected.description: Edges that must be present. Missing one is an incompleteness failure.

forbidden.description: Phantom edges this case is built to provoke. Returning one is a correctness failure.

reason.description: For `forbidden`: which shortcut would produce this edge. For `expected`: why it is reachable only with real resolution.

admissibility.description: What the system under test is permitted to CLAIM about this fact, independently of whether it got the fact right. Scored separately: a wrong answer correctly caveated is a miss; a wrong answer presented as complete is a false-safe.

may_claim_complete.description: False when no sound static analysis can enumerate this relation exhaustively for this case.

may_claim_safe_to_rename.description: False when a rename driven by this relation would miss sites or be overwritten downstream.
